summary:
SpatialWorkingSet.create copied each chunk's bucket list once per member entry (values @ [ index ]) and did a map lookup plus insertion per membership, so construction was quadratic in the population of one chunk: 40,000 entries in one 64-unit chunk took about 4.8 s and 25.7 GB of allocation per create, and 100,000 spread entries about 370 ms. Rendering#1473 (Delivery #1472, merge 9567e8f8) collects members in one forward pass over a hash table, records chunk keys in order of first appearance and adds each key to the immutable map once with its ordinals in ascending order. Public API, ordering, counters, refusal order and the query path are unchanged. CLR before/after on one shared 3-CPU dev host, same harness, ABBA, identical selections and counters: 40,000 in one chunk 4,827 to 36.4 ms (25,689 to 65 MB); 20,000 in one chunk 1,150 to 12.6 ms; regular grid 100,000 308 to 130 ms; mixed chunk-spanning 20,000 55.9 to 14.0 ms; spread 100,000 370 to 275 ms; allocation fell in every cell; query cost unchanged (largest median ratio 1.053 over 36 cells).

Reusable lessons. First, the key insertion order of an immutable balanced map fixes its shape and so lookup cost: a first design that visited entries last-to-first and prepended into the same map removed the quadratic term but inserted keys in descending order and made some queries 10 to 30 percent slower, consistently in both runs. When only the value construction is wrong, keep the key insertion order (collect per key in a hash table, then add keys in first-appearance order). Second, query results here are sorted by ordinal, so a bucket left in the wrong order is invisible to query-level oracles; pin it with a structure control that reads the private buckets and compares them with an independent direct scan, and include a bucket larger than any size-dependent branch (a mutant that reversed only buckets over 1,000 members survived until such a bucket was added). Third, measure the adverse side of a construction change on the query path too, with the same harness for both arms, rather than inferring it.

Limits: construction is paid when an index is created, not per frame; the synthetic 250-entry grid gains 0.13 ms per create, so no product speedup is claimed and the large gains apply to dense populations. One shared development host; no timing threshold, hosted benchmark, Home B1-B8 verdict, publication, installed adoption or GPU claim follows. Incremental index updates and the other source hotspots remain open.
title: Spatial index bucket construction was quadratic per chunk and key insertion order affects query cost
